Summary: Deuteronomy 6:13 commands fear of the LORD: 'Thou shalt fear the LORD thy God, and serve him.' Fear here is reverent obedience, joined to service and to swearing by his name alone.
Commandment: Fear the LORD your God, and serve him.
Application: Fear belongs with serving and cleaving to the God who brought Israel out of Egypt and keeps covenant (Deuteronomy 10:20-22).
Purpose: Scripture's stated context: fear belongs with serving and cleaving to the God who brought Israel out of Egypt and keeps covenant (Deuteronomy 10:20-22).
Function: Deuteronomy 6:13 commands fear of the LORD: 'Thou shalt fear the LORD thy God, and serve him.' This binds in every age: a duty of conduct, not a rule of Israel's civil code. Scripture gives the context: fear belongs with serving and cleaving to the God who brought Israel out of Egypt and keeps covenant. No particular evil is named here; its work was fearing the LORD, not restraint.
